mission.description: A Terraform config was written to create a local file, but it has a syntax error and won't even parse.
mission.name: Your First Resource
mission.objective: Fix the HCL syntax error so that `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The config uses the wrong keyword for declaring an output value — it says `outputs` instead of `output`.
mission.name: Block Identity Crisis
mission.objective: Fix the block keyword so the output is declared correctly and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: `terraform init` fails because the required provider version does not exist.
mission.name: The Missing Provider
mission.objective: Fix the `required_providers` version constraint so that `terraform init` can download the provider.

mission.description: The provider version constraint uses an invalid operator that Terraform doesn't recognise.
mission.name: Syntax Smash
mission.objective: Fix the version constraint operator so `terraform init` succeeds.

mission.description: Someone deleted the entire `terraform {}` settings block. Terraform can still run but the provider source is unspecified, causing init to fail.
mission.name: Block Disappeared
mission.objective: Add back the `terraform {}` block with the correct `required_providers` entry for `hashicorp/local`.

mission.description: The `required_version` constraint demands a Terraform version that doesn't exist, blocking all operations.
mission.name: Version Lockout
mission.objective: Fix `required_version` to allow the currently installed Terraform version.

mission.description: A string value was entered with a mismatched quote — the string never closes, causing a parse error.
mission.name: Quote Disaster
mission.objective: Fix the unclosed string literal so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A heredoc string is using `<<EOF` (non-indented) but the closing marker is indented, causing a parse error.
mission.name: Heredoc Headache
mission.objective: Fix the heredoc so it uses `<<-EOF` (indented form) and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A string interpolation expression uses `$()` instead of `${}`, which is shell syntax, not HCL.
mission.name: Interpolation Implosion
mission.objective: Fix the interpolation syntax so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A multi-line string value was written without a heredoc — it spans two lines inside regular quotes, which is invalid HCL.
mission.name: String Escape
mission.objective: Convert the broken multi-line string to a valid heredoc so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `random_string` resource has its `length` attribute set to a string `"16"` instead of a number `16`.
mission.name: Type Confusion
mission.objective: Fix the type so `length` receives a number and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The `special` attribute is set to the string `"true"` instead of the boolean `true`, causing a type error.
mission.name: True or False?
mission.objective: Fix the boolean attribute so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable marked `nullable = false` has a `default = null`. This combination is invalid — a non-nullable variable cannot default to null.
mission.name: Null and Void
mission.objective: Fix the variable declaration so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `/* block comment */` was left unclosed inside an attribute assignment, corrupting the entire config.
mission.name: Comment Catastrophe
mission.objective: Fix or remove the unclosed block comment so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The `templatefile()` function references a template file that doesn't exist at the given path.
mission.name: File Not Found
mission.objective: Create the missing template file (or fix the path) so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: `main.tf` references a variable defined in `variables.tf`, but `variables.tf` is missing from the config.
mission.name: Split Personality
mission.objective: Create `variables.tf` with the correct variable declaration so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The `locals` block declares the same key `app_name` twice, which is not allowed.
mission.name: Double Vision
mission.objective: Fix the duplicate local value so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: Two local values reference each other, creating a dependency cycle that Terraform cannot resolve.
mission.name: Circular Reference
mission.objective: Break the cycle by rewriting the locals so each one is independently computable. `terraform validate` must pass.

mission.description: The resource has an invalid name that starts with a digit, which is not allowed in HCL identifiers.
mission.name: The Name Game
mission.objective: Rename the resource with a valid identifier so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A provider alias is declared but the resource uses a wrong alias reference, causing a validation error.
mission.name: Alias Identity
mission.objective: Fix the `provider` meta-argument on the resource to correctly reference the declared alias.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource points its `filename` at a deeply nested directory `/tmp/nonexistent/dir/config.txt` that Terraform will not create automatically. The apply fails because the parent directories do not exist.
mission.name: The Unreachable Path
mission.objective: Fix the `filename` attribute so `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource uses `content_base64` with a plain text string instead of a properly base64-encoded value. This causes an apply-time error.
mission.name: Base64 or Bust
mission.objective: Fix the resource so it uses the correct attribute for plain text content.

mission.description: A `local_sensitive_file` resource is declared without the required `file_permission` attribute. `terraform validate` reports a missing required argument.
mission.name: Permission Denied by Design
mission.objective: Add the missing `file_permission` attribute so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `random_string` resource has `length = 0`, which is invalid. The minimum allowed length is 1.
mission.name: Zero is Nothing
mission.objective: Fix the `length` attribute so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `random_string` resource sets `special = true` and `override_special = ""` (an empty string). This forces special characters to come from an empty set, causing an apply-time error.
mission.name: Special Characters Gone Wrong
mission.objective: Fix `override_special` so that `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: A `random_integer` resource has `min = 100` and `max = 10`. The minimum value is greater than the maximum, which is invalid.
mission.name: Min Greater Than Max
mission.objective: Swap `min` and `max` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `random_password` resource has `length = 5` but `min_upper = 2`, `min_lower = 2`, `min_numeric = 2`. The sum of minimums (6) exceeds the total length (5), which is impossible to satisfy.
mission.name: More Than the Sum of Its Parts
mission.objective: Increase `length` so `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: An output references `random_uuid.app_id.result`, but `random_uuid` does not have a `result` attribute. The correct attribute is `id`.
mission.name: UUID Got the Wrong Attribute
mission.objective: Fix the output reference so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `random_pet` resource has `separator = 123` — a number instead of a string. HCL type checking catches this mismatch.
mission.name: A Number is Not a Separator
mission.objective: Fix the `separator` attribute type so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `null_resource` uses `triggers = { version = 1 }` with a number value. `triggers` is typed as `map(string)`, so all values must be strings.
mission.name: Triggers Expect Strings
mission.objective: Fix the `triggers` map so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `null_resource` provisioner runs `echoo hello` — a typo in the shell command. The provisioner fails at apply time because `echoo` is not a valid command.
mission.name: Echoo is Not a Command
mission.objective: Fix the typo in the provisioner command so `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: A `tls_private_key` resource uses `algorithm = "DSA"`, which is not supported. Only RSA, ECDSA, and ED25519 are valid algorithms.
mission.name: DSA is Not Supported
mission.objective: Fix the `algorithm` attribute so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `tls_self_signed_cert` resource has `validity_period_hours = -1`. A certificate cannot have a negative validity period.
mission.name: Negative Time Makes No Sense
mission.objective: Fix `validity_period_hours` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `tls_cert_request` resource is missing the required `subject {}` block. Without a subject, the Certificate Signing Request (CSR) cannot be generated.
mission.name: The Missing Subject
mission.objective: Add the `subject {}` block so `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource uses `"${random_string.token}"` in its content — missing the `.result` attribute. This references the whole resource object, not the string value.
mission.name: Missing the Attribute Dot
mission.objective: Fix the reference so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: Two `local_file` resources exist. The second references `local_file.first.path` to get the first file's path — but `local_file` does not expose a `.path` attribute. The correct attribute is `.filename`.
mission.name: The Wrong Breadcrumb
mission.objective: Fix the attribute reference so `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource has `depends_on = [local_file.nonexistent]`, referencing a resource that does not exist in the configuration.
mission.name: Depending on a Ghost
mission.objective: Fix or remove the bogus `depends_on` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A resource has `timeouts { create = 600 }` with a raw number. Terraform timeout values must be duration strings like `"10m"` or `"1h"`.
mission.name: Duration is a String, Not a Number
mission.objective: Fix the `timeouts` block so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A resource has `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. When you try to plan a destroy, Terraform exits with error code 1 because the lifecycle rule blocks it.
mission.name: Protected from Deletion
mission.objective: Set `prevent_destroy = false` so that `terraform plan -destroy` exits 0 or 2 (not 1).

mission.description: A `local_file` resource has `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [nonexistent_attr] }`, referencing an attribute that does not exist on `local_file`.
mission.name: Ignoring What Doesn't Exist
mission.objective: Fix `ignore_changes` to reference a valid attribute (or use `all`) so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable is declared as `type = number` but its default is `"hello"` — a string. Terraform's type checker rejects this mismatch.
mission.name: Type Mismatch: String Masquerading as Number
mission.objective: Fix the type declaration so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable has `type = number` and `default = "42"` — the number is wrapped in quotes, making it a string. Terraform may coerce this, but it is considered a type mismatch and should be corrected.
mission.name: Quoted Numbers Are Not Numbers
mission.objective: Fix the default value so it is an unquoted number and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable has `type = bool` and `default = "false"` — the boolean is wrapped in quotes, making it a string. Fix the default value.
mission.name: False is Not a String
mission.objective: Fix the default value so it is an unquoted boolean and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable is declared as `type = list(string)` but its default contains a number: `["a", "b", 3]`. The number `3` must be the string `"3"`.
mission.name: One Number Ruins the List
mission.objective: Fix the default value so all elements are strings and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable is declared as `type = map(string)` but its default has mixed types: `{ a = "x", b = 2 }`. The value `2` is a number, not a string.
mission.name: Mixed Types in a String Map
mission.objective: Fix the default value so all map values are strings and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable has `type = object({ name = string, port = number })` but its default is `{ name = "app" }` — missing the required `port` key.
mission.name: Object Missing a Required Key
mission.objective: Add the missing `port` key to the default so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable has `type = set(string)` with `default = ["a", "b", "a"]`. Sets do not allow duplicate elements — the duplicate `"a"` is invalid.
mission.name: Sets Don't Allow Duplicates
mission.objective: Remove the duplicate element so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable has `type = tuple([string, number])` but `default = ["hello", "world"]`. The second element should be a number, not a string.
mission.name: Tuples Need Exact Types
mission.objective: Fix the second element so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable has a `validation` block with `condition = var.env == "prod"`. The default value is `"dev"`, so the condition is always false and terraform plan fails with the validation error message.
mission.name: The Condition Always Fails
mission.objective: Fix the `condition` to accept `"dev"`, `"staging"`, and `"prod"` so `terraform plan` succeeds with the default value.

mission.description: A variable has a `validation` block with `error_message = ""` — an empty string. Terraform requires `error_message` to be a non-empty string.
mission.name: An Error Message Must Have Words
mission.objective: Add a meaningful `error_message` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A variable has `nullable = false` and `default = null`. This is a contradiction: `nullable = false` means the variable can never be null, but `default = null` sets the default to null.
mission.name: Null and Non-Nullable Don't Mix
mission.objective: Fix the contradiction so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: An output block has `sensitive = "true"` — a string instead of the boolean `true`. Terraform's type checker rejects the string.
mission.name: Sensitive is a Bool, Not a String
mission.objective: Fix `sensitive` to be a boolean so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: An output references `local_file.config.content`, but `local_file` does not expose `content` as a readable exported attribute. Use `.filename` instead.
mission.name: Local File Has No Content Output
mission.objective: Fix the output reference so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: An `output` block has `depends_on = [local_file.nonexistent]`, referencing a resource that does not exist in the configuration.
mission.name: Output Depends on a Ghost
mission.objective: Fix or remove the bogus `depends_on` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `terraform.tfvars` file contains `environment "production"` — missing the `=` assignment operator. This is a syntax error that causes `terraform plan` to fail.
mission.name: The tfvars Assignment Operator
mission.objective: Fix the syntax in `terraform.tfvars` so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A variable `environment` is declared as `type = number` but the intended values are strings like `"dev"` and `"staging"`. Running `terraform plan -var="environment=staging"` fails with a type error.
mission.name: The Wrong Type Blocks the Flag
mission.objective: Fix the variable type so `terraform plan -var="environment=staging"` succeeds.

mission.description: An output tries to access `var.config.nonexistent_key` on an object variable that has no such key. The correct key is `name`.
mission.name: Accessing a Key That Doesn't Exist
mission.objective: Fix the output to use the correct key so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: An output has a `precondition` block requiring `var.port >= 1024`, but the variable's default is `80` — which fails the precondition. `terraform plan` exits with an error.
mission.name: Precondition Fails on Its Own Default
mission.objective: Change the variable default to `8080` so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A config creates three `random_string` resources (alpha, beta, gamma) but the output references a nonexistent resource named `delta`.
mission.name: State Inspector
mission.objective: Fix the output so it references `random_string.gamma.result`. Then `terraform apply` must succeed and the output must be populated.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource is declared but the `filename` attribute is missing, preventing apply. After the fix the validator will rename the resource in state with `terraform state mv`.
mission.name: State Mover
mission.objective: Add the missing `filename` attribute so `terraform apply` succeeds. The validator will then run `terraform state mv local_file.old_name local_file.new_name` and verify the new address exists in state.

mission.description: Two `local_file` resources form a circular dependency — each references the other's filename in its content. This makes `terraform apply` impossible.
mission.name: State Eraser
mission.objective: Break the circular dependency so `terraform apply` succeeds. The validator will then run `terraform state rm local_file.file_b` and verify the result.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource uses `var.file_contents` (with a trailing 's') but the variable is declared as `var.file_content`. Fix the reference so apply works, then the validator will simulate drift and verify it is detected.
mission.name: Drift Detector
mission.objective: Fix the variable reference from `var.file_contents` to `var.file_content`. After apply, the validator modifies the file externally and checks that `terraform plan -detailed-exitcode` returns exit code 2 (drift detected).

mission.description: A `local_file` resource is declared but its `filename` points to the wrong path. The validator will create `/tmp/tm_existing.txt` and attempt to import it — the config filename must match.
mission.name: Resource Importer
mission.objective: Change the `filename` to `/tmp/tm_existing.txt` so the import command succeeds and the resource appears in state.

mission.description: Terraform 1.5 introduced `import {}` blocks for declarative imports. The config has an `import` block with the wrong file path as the resource ID.
mission.name: Declarative Import
mission.objective: Fix the `import` block's `id` to match `"${path.module}/config.txt"` — the same path used in the resource's `filename` attribute.

mission.description: A resource was renamed from `old_name` to `new_name` in the configuration, but the `moved {}` block was forgotten. Without it, Terraform plans a destroy+create instead of a rename.
mission.name: The Moved Block
mission.objective: Add a `moved { from = local_file.old_name  to = local_file.new_name }` block so `terraform apply` performs an in-place rename rather than destroy+create.

mission.description: The `terraform {}` block configures a local backend with a path that points to a nonexistent directory: `../../nonexistent/terraform.tfstate`. Terraform cannot initialise.
mission.name: Backend Basics
mission.objective: Fix the backend `path` to use `"terraform.tfstate"` (in the current directory) so `terraform init` and `terraform plan` succeed.

mission.description: The `.terraform.lock.hcl` file contains deliberately wrong provider hashes. Terraform detects the mismatch and refuses to use the cached provider.
mission.name: Lock File Chaos
mission.objective: Delete the broken `.terraform.lock.hcl` file so `terraform init -upgrade` can regenerate it with the correct hashes.

mission.description: A `null_resource` has a trigger version that wasn't updated when the application version bumped from v1 to v2. Terraform doesn't detect the change and won't replace the resource.
mission.name: Force Replace
mission.objective: Update the trigger value from `"v1"` to `"v2"` so that `terraform plan` shows the resource will be replaced.

mission.description: Three chained resources A → B → C exist, but C references `local_file.resource_b.content_md5` which is not an exported attribute of `local_file`.
mission.name: Targeted Apply
mission.objective: Fix the reference in `resource_c` from `.content_md5` to `.filename` so `terraform apply` succeeds for all three resources.

mission.description: Five `random_string` resources are declared, but one is named `count` — a reserved Terraform meta-argument. This causes a validation error.
mission.name: State List and Naming
mission.objective: Rename the `count` resource to a valid name (e.g., `epsilon`) so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The `backend "local"` block references `var.state_path` — but variables cannot be used in backend configuration blocks. Terraform reports an error during init.
mission.name: Partial Backend Config
mission.objective: Replace `var.state_path` with the literal string `"terraform.tfstate"` in the backend block so `terraform init` succeeds.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource has an output that references `local_file.data.size` — an attribute that doesn't exist on `local_file`. Fix it so apply and `terraform apply -refresh-only` both work.
mission.name: Refresh Only
mission.objective: Change the output to reference `local_file.data.filename` (a valid attribute) so the config applies and refresh-only mode works.

mission.description: A `random_password` resource has `length = 0`, which is invalid. Fix the length so apply succeeds. The validator will then use `terraform state pull` to inspect the state JSON.
mission.name: State Pull Inspector
mission.objective: Change `length = 0` to a valid value (e.g., `16`) so `terraform apply` succeeds and `terraform state pull` can read the state.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource has `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`. This blocks any destroy operation. The validator checks that a destroy plan succeeds — so `prevent_destroy` must be removed or set to `false`.
mission.name: Prevent Destroy Removal
mission.objective: Change `prevent_destroy = true` to `prevent_destroy = false` (or remove the lifecycle block) so `terraform plan -destroy` succeeds.

mission.description: A `null_resource` is named `job` but the validator tries to taint `null_resource.task`. Rename the resource to `task` so the taint command succeeds.
mission.name: Tainted Resource
mission.objective: Rename the `null_resource` from `job` to `task` so `terraform taint null_resource.task` succeeds and the plan shows replacement.

mission.description: The resource is declared with type `local_files` (with a trailing 's') — this provider resource type doesn't exist. Fix the type so apply works, then the validator runs `terraform state rm`.
mission.name: State Remove
mission.objective: Change `resource "local_files" "config"` to `resource "local_file" "config"` (remove the trailing 's') so apply succeeds and `terraform state rm` can clean it up.

mission.description: A `terraform_remote_state` data source points to `/nonexistent/path/terraform.tfstate`. The validator creates `other.tfstate` in the working directory — fix the path to point there.
mission.name: Output from Remote State
mission.objective: Change the `path` in the `terraform_remote_state` config to `"${path.module}/other.tfstate"` so Terraform can read outputs from the sibling state file.

mission.description: Three resources are declared, but `config_b` uses the invalid type `local_files`. Fix both the resource type and the output reference so all three resources apply and appear in state.
mission.name: State Surgery
mission.objective: Change `resource "local_files" "config_b"` to `resource "local_file" "config_b"` and fix the output. `terraform apply` must succeed with all 3 resources in state.

mission.description: `format("%s-%d", "app")` is called with only one argument but the format string expects two values — one `%s` (string) and one `%d` (integer).
mission.name: Format Function
mission.objective: Add the missing second argument so the call becomes `format("%s-%d", "app", 1)` and `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: `formatlist("%s-%s", ["a","b"])` has two `%s` placeholders but only one list argument. `formatlist` requires a list for each placeholder.
mission.name: Format List
mission.objective: Fix the call to use a single placeholder: `formatlist("%s", ["a","b"])` so the output is `["a", "b"]`.

mission.description: `replace(var.name, "/[^a-z]/", "-", "g")` is called with 4 arguments, but `replace()` only accepts 3. The trailing `"g"` flag is not a valid parameter.
mission.name: String Functions
mission.objective: Remove the extra `"g"` argument so the call is `replace(var.name, "/[^a-z]/", "-")` and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The string `"a;b;c"` uses semicolons as separators, but `split(",", ...)` uses a comma. The split returns the whole string as one element instead of three.
mission.name: Split and Join
mission.objective: Fix the separator in `split()` from `","` to `";"` so the output `result` equals `"a-b-c"`.

mission.description: `length(var.items.nonexistent)` tries to access a key `nonexistent` on the map before calling `length()`. This fails because the key doesn't exist.
mission.name: Length Function
mission.objective: Fix the count expression to use `length(var.items)` — the length of the whole map — so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: `lookup(var.config, "port")` is called with only 2 arguments. The `lookup()` function requires a third argument: the default value to return if the key is not found.
mission.name: Lookup Function
mission.objective: Add a default value: `lookup(var.config, "port", 8080)` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: `index(["a","b","c"], "d")` tries to find `"d"` in the list, but `"d"` is not present. `index()` throws an error when the value is not found.
mission.name: Contains vs Index
mission.objective: Replace the `index()` call with `contains()` which safely returns `false` when the value is absent. Update the local and output names accordingly.

mission.description: `flatten([["a","b"], "c"])` mixes a list and a bare string at the top level. `flatten()` expects all top-level elements to be lists.
mission.name: Flatten
mission.objective: Wrap `"c"` in a list: `flatten([["a","b"], ["c"]])` so the output is `["a", "b", "c"]`.

mission.description: `merge(["a","b"], ["c"])` uses `merge()` on lists, but `merge()` is designed for maps. Use `concat()` to combine lists.
mission.name: Concat vs Merge
mission.objective: Replace `merge(...)` with `concat(["a","b"], ["c"])` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: `setunion(["a","b"], ["c"])` passes lists to `setunion()`, but it expects sets. Convert the lists with `toset()` first.
mission.name: Set Union
mission.objective: Wrap both arguments with `toset()`: `setunion(toset(["a","b"]), toset(["c"]))` so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: The `local.config` map uses `timestamp()` which produces a dynamic, non-deterministic value. This causes plan instability — the JSON output changes on every run. Replace it with a static map.
mission.name: JSON Encode
mission.objective: Remove `timestamp()` and replace it with a static string value so `jsonencode(local.config)` produces stable, valid JSON.

mission.description: `templatefile()` is called with `{ name = var.app }` but the template `app.tpl` uses `${app_name}`. The variable name in the map doesn't match the placeholder in the template.
mission.name: Template File
mission.objective: Change the vars map key from `name` to `app_name` so the template renders correctly and the output file contains `"myapp"`.

mission.description: `cidrsubnet("10.0.0.0/24", 8, 1)` tries to add 8 bits to a /24 network, creating a /32. A /32 is a single host address — subnet index 1 overflows.
mission.name: CIDR Subnet
mission.objective: Change the base to `"10.0.0.0/16"` so there is room to add 8 bits (creating /24 subnets) and index 1 is valid.

mission.description: `tolist(var.my_map)` tries to convert a `map(string)` to a list, but `tolist()` only works on collections that are already list-like (tuples). Maps must use `values()` to extract their values as a list.
mission.name: Type Conversion
mission.objective: Replace `tolist(var.my_map)` with `values(var.my_map)` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: `var.enabled ? "yes" : 0` mixes types — the true branch is a string `"yes"` but the false branch is a number `0`. Both branches must be the same type.
mission.name: Ternary Operator
mission.objective: Fix the false branch to be a string: `var.enabled ? "yes" : "no"` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: `[for item in var.items : item.value]` tries to access `.value` on each string element, but `var.items` is `list(string)` — strings have no `.value` attribute.
mission.name: For Expression List
mission.objective: Fix the for expression to transform strings directly: `[for item in var.items : upper(item)]` so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: `{for k, v in var.tags : k, v}` uses a comma between the key and value expressions. Map-producing for expressions require `=>` as the separator.
mission.name: For Expression Map
mission.objective: Change the comma to `=>`: `{for k, v in var.tags : k => v}` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: `[for x in var.items : x if x > 10]` compares string elements to a number. `var.items` is `list(string)` — strings cannot be compared to numbers with `>`.
mission.name: For Expression Filter
mission.objective: Fix the filter by converting each element with `tonumber()`: `[for x in var.items : x if tonumber(x) > 10]` so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: `local_file.config[*].filename` uses a splat expression on a single resource that has no `count` or `for_each`. Splat expressions require the resource to produce a list (i.e., use `count`).
mission.name: Splat Expression
mission.objective: Add `count = 2` to the `local_file.config` resource (and update `content` and `filename` to use `count.index`) so the splat expression is valid.

mission.description: `%{if var.debug}` requires a boolean condition, but `var.debug` is declared as `type = string` with default `"true"`. String `"true"` is not a bool.
mission.name: String Directives
mission.objective: Change the variable type from `string` to `bool` and the default from `"true"` to `true` so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A root module calls a child module, but the `source` path is wrong — it points to `../hello` instead of the correct relative path.
mission.name: Wrong Module Path
mission.objective: Fix the `source` argument in the module block so `terraform init && terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: The child module declares a required variable `app_name` with no default value, but the root module call forgets to pass it.
mission.name: Missing Module Input
mission.objective: Add the missing `app_name` argument to the module call so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The child module expects `var.port` as a `number`, but the root passes a string `"8080"` (with quotes).
mission.name: Type Mismatch at the Module Boundary
mission.objective: Fix the type mismatch so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The root module references `module.mymod.wrong_output` — an output that doesn't exist in the child module.
mission.name: Wrong Output Name
mission.objective: Fix the output reference to use the correct output name `file_path`.

mission.description: The child module creates a file but declares no `output` block. The root tries to reference `module.mymod.filename` which doesn't exist.
mission.name: Missing Output Declaration
mission.objective: Add an `output "filename"` block to the child module so the root can access the value.

mission.description: A module is called with `count = 2` but no `name` argument is passed. The child module requires `name`, so validation fails.
mission.name: Count Without count.index
mission.objective: Pass `name = "app-${count.index}"` to the module so each instance gets a unique name.

mission.description: A module is called with `for_each = toset(["a", "b"])`. The root output references `module.mods.file_path` instead of `module.mods["a"].file_path` — module instances must be addressed by key.
mission.name: for_each Module Reference
mission.objective: Fix the output so it correctly references a specific `for_each` module instance.

mission.description: `depends_on = [module.nonexistent]` references a module that doesn't exist, causing a validation error.
mission.name: Broken depends_on Reference
mission.objective: Remove or fix the `depends_on` so it references a real module or resource.

mission.description: The root passes `providers = { local = local.wrong_alias }` to the child module, but the alias `local.wrong_alias` is not declared in the root provider config.
mission.name: Wrong Provider Alias in Module
mission.objective: Fix the `providers` map to reference the declared provider alias `local.primary`.

mission.description: A child module uses `path.root` where it should use `path.module`. `path.root` is the root module's directory — not where the child module lives.
mission.name: path.root vs path.module
mission.objective: Replace `path.root` with `path.module` inside the child module.

mission.description: A child module takes a `sensitive` variable and returns it as an output, but the output doesn't declare `sensitive = true`. Terraform will error because a sensitive value flows into a non-sensitive output.
mission.name: Sensitive Output Leak
mission.objective: Add `sensitive = true` to the child module's output block.

mission.description: The child module has a `validation` block that only allows `env == "valid"`. The root passes `env = "prod"` which is a real environment, but the validation rejects it.
mission.name: Overly Strict Validation
mission.objective: Fix the validation condition to allow `dev`, `staging`, and `prod`.

mission.description: A child module resource has a `precondition` that requires `var.item_count > 10`, but the variable defaults to `1`. The precondition always fails.
mission.name: Impossible Precondition
mission.objective: Fix the precondition to `var.item_count > 0` so the default value passes.

mission.description: An output has a `postcondition` whose condition is `self.value == ""` — it passes only when the value IS empty, which is backwards. The intent is to ensure the value is NOT empty.
mission.name: Inverted Postcondition
mission.objective: Fix the postcondition to `self.value != ""`.

mission.description: A module was renamed from `module.old` to `module.new` in the config, but no `moved` block was added. Terraform will plan to destroy the old instance and create a new one instead of renaming in state.
mission.name: Renamed Module Without moved Block
mission.objective: Add a `moved` block to tell Terraform the module was renamed, preventing destroy/create.

mission.description: Module A outputs `config_path`. The root passes that to Module B as `config_file`, but Module B's variable is named `config_path`, not `config_file`.
mission.name: Module Composition Mismatch
mission.objective: Fix the root to pass `config_path` (not `config_file`) to Module B.

mission.description: The root tries to source a module from a Git URL that doesn't exist. `terraform init` fails because the remote source is unreachable.
mission.name: Unreachable Module Source
mission.objective: Change the module `source` to the local path `./modules/local` so `terraform init` succeeds.

mission.description: The child module uses `file_content` instead of `content` for the `local_file` resource — an invalid argument name that causes validation to fail.
mission.name: Broken Child Module Syntax
mission.objective: Fix the `local_file` argument name from `file_content` to `content`.

mission.description: A `.tftest.hcl` file uses `command = apply_all` which is not a valid `terraform test` command. Valid values are `apply` and `plan`.
mission.name: Invalid Test Command
mission.objective: Fix the test command to `apply` so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: The test asserts that `output.result == "wrong"`, but the module actually outputs `"correct"`. The assertion is inverted.
mission.name: Wrong Test Assertion
mission.objective: Fix the assertion condition to `output.result == "correct"` so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: `count = 3` creates three instances of a `local_file` resource, but all three use the same `filename = "config.txt"` — no `count.index` is used. The three instances would all write to the same file.
mission.name: Three Files, Same Name
mission.objective: Use `count.index` in the `filename` so each instance gets a unique filename like `config-0.txt`, `config-1.txt`, `config-2.txt`.

mission.description: `count = var.enabled ? 1 : 0` conditionally creates a resource. With `enabled = false`, `count = 0` and no instance exists. The output references `local_file.config[0].filename` — which errors when count is 0.
mission.name: Referencing a Zero-Count Resource
mission.objective: Fix the output to use `try(local_file.config[0].filename, "")` so it safely handles the count=0 case.

mission.description: Three files are created: `file-0.txt`, `file-1.txt`, `file-2.txt`. The output expects files named `file-1.txt` through `file-3.txt` — an off-by-one in the output expression.
mission.name: Off-by-One Output
mission.objective: Fix the output to correctly reference `file-0.txt` through `file-2.txt` using `local_file.files[*].filename`.

mission.description: `count = var.enabled ? 1 : 0` requires `var.enabled` to be a `bool`. The variable is declared as `type = string` with `default = "true"`. Terraform cannot use a string in the ternary condition.
mission.name: String Bool in Conditional Count
mission.objective: Change `var.enabled` to `type = bool` with `default = true` so the conditional works correctly.

mission.description: `local_file.config` is a `count`-based resource. The output references `local_file.config.filename` as if it were a single resource — but you need `[*]` to get all filenames.
mission.name: Missing Splat on Count Resource
mission.objective: Fix the output to `value = local_file.config[*].filename`.

mission.description: `for_each = toset(var.names)` with `var.names = ["a", "b", "a"]` works fine because `toset()` deduplicates. However, the variable default is set to a list with a duplicate `"a"`. The config works but produces only 2 instances instead of the expected 3. The real bug: the variable default should not have duplicates.
mission.name: Duplicate in toset()
mission.objective: Remove the duplicate `"a"` from `var.names` default so the intent is clear and the set has exactly 2 unique values.

mission.description: `for_each = var.services` iterates over a map. Inside the resource, `each.name` is used — but `each.name` doesn't exist. The correct attribute is `each.key`.
mission.name: each.name vs each.key
mission.objective: Replace `each.name` with `each.key` so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `for` expression iterates over `local_file.configs` and accesses `.path` — but the `local_file` resource attribute is `.filename`, not `.path`.
mission.name: Wrong Attribute in for Expression
mission.objective: Fix the for expression to use `.filename` instead of `.path`.

mission.description: Resource B tries `for_each = local_file.configs` — passing a resource collection directly. Terraform requires `for_each` to be a map or set, not a resource collection object. Fix it by converting the resource to a proper map with a `for` expression.
mission.name: Resource as for_each Value
mission.objective: Change `for_each` to `{ for k, v in local_file.configs : k => v.filename }` to produce a valid map.

mission.description: `for_each = var.items` where `var.items = {}` creates zero resources. The output tries to access `local_file.items["main"].filename` which doesn't exist when the map is empty.
mission.name: Empty for_each Map
mission.objective: Add a default entry `main = "default"` to `var.items` so the resource is created and the output works.

mission.description: A module uses `count = 2`. The caller references `module.mymod["key"]` — but `count`-based modules use numeric indices like `[0]`, not string keys.
mission.name: count vs for_each Addressing
mission.objective: Fix the output to reference `module.mymod[0].file_path` instead of `module.mymod["key"].file_path`.

mission.description: A `dynamic` block is named `"setting"` but the resource uses nested blocks called `"settings"` (plural). The dynamic block name must match the nested block name exactly.
mission.name: Wrong Dynamic Block Name
mission.objective: Rename the `dynamic "setting"` block to `dynamic "settings"` to match the nested block name.

mission.description: A `dynamic` block iterates over `var.tags` but the `content` block uses `each.value.name` instead of the correct iterator `tag.value` (the dynamic block's iterator is named after the block label, not `each`).
mission.name: Wrong Iterator in Dynamic Block
mission.objective: Replace `each.value.name` with `tag.key` and `each.value.value` with `tag.value` inside the dynamic block content.

mission.description: A pattern `for_each = var.env != null ? [var.env] : []` is used to optionally include a block. But `var.env` is declared `nullable = false`, so it can never be null — the optional logic is broken. Fix: set `nullable = true`.
mission.name: Non-nullable Variable in Optional Block
mission.objective: Change `nullable = false` to `nullable = true` on `var.env` so the null check works.

mission.description: A `for_each` is fed by a nested `for` expression over services and ports. The nested for produces a list of lists, not a flat list. Wrapping with `flatten()` fixes it.
mission.name: Nested for Expression Needs flatten()
mission.objective: Wrap the nested `for` expression in `flatten()` so `toset()` receives a flat list.

mission.description: `for_each` uses `random_string.id.result` as a key — but `random_string.result` is only known after apply, not during planning. Terraform rejects this because `for_each` keys must be known at plan time.
mission.name: for_each Key Unknown at Plan Time
mission.objective: Replace the `random_string` key with a static string key so the plan succeeds.

mission.description: Resources were migrated from `count`-based to `for_each`-based, renaming from `local_file.items[0]` and `local_file.items[1]` to `local_file.items["alpha"]` and `local_file.items["beta"]`. Without `moved` blocks, Terraform will destroy and recreate.
mission.name: count to for_each Migration
mission.objective: Add `moved` blocks to map the old count indices to the new for_each keys.

mission.description: A module is called with `count = var.enabled ? 1 : 0`. The output references `module.mymod.file_path` — but with `count`, module instances are addressed as `module.mymod[0].file_path`.
mission.name: Conditional Module Output Reference
mission.objective: Fix the output to use `module.mymod[0].file_path` (or `try(module.mymod[0].file_path, "")`  for safety).

mission.description: A data source reads a local file, but the path is wrong and Terraform cannot find it.
mission.name: File Not Found
mission.objective: Fix the filename path so the data source can locate `data.txt` and `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A data source reads a README file, but the output uses the Base64-encoded attribute instead of plain text.
mission.name: Lost in Encoding
mission.objective: Fix the output to use `content` instead of `content_base64` so the output shows readable text.

mission.description: An HTTP data source has a malformed URL — it is missing the `https://` scheme.
mission.name: Invalid URL Scheme
mission.objective: Fix the URL so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A data source reads a JSON file and `jsondecode` is used to extract a value, but the wrong key is referenced.
mission.name: Wrong JSON Key
mission.objective: Fix the key used in `jsondecode` so the output resolves correctly and `terraform plan` passes.

mission.description: An external data source calls a Python script, but the script prints plain text instead of valid JSON.
mission.name: Script Doesn't Speak JSON
mission.objective: Fix `get_info.py` so it outputs valid JSON, allowing `terraform plan` to succeed.

mission.description: The external data source references a binary that does not exist on the system.
mission.name: Missing Executable
mission.objective: Fix the `program` list to use a valid executable that outputs JSON, so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A data source reads a file that is created by a `local_file` resource, but the data source tries to read the file before it is created.
mission.name: Ordering Matters
mission.objective: Add `depends_on` to the data source so it waits for the resource to create the file first, and `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: A data source uses `count = 3` to read three config files, but the output references index `[3]` which is out of range.
mission.name: Index Out of Range
mission.objective: Fix the out-of-range index so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A data source uses `for_each` over a set of filenames, but the output references the data source without a key.
mission.name: Missing Map Key
mission.objective: Fix the output to use the correct `for_each` key syntax so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A child module reads a data source and exposes the result as an output. The root module references the wrong output name.
mission.name: Module Output Name Mismatch
mission.objective: Fix the root module's output reference to use the correct output name and `terraform plan` passes.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource and a data source both reference the same file. The data source uses the wrong attribute after the file content changes.
mission.name: Stale Data Source
mission.objective: Fix the data source attribute reference and run `terraform plan -refresh-only` to verify the data source reflects current state.

mission.description: A `terraform_remote_state` data source points to a local state file, but the path is incorrect.
mission.name: Remote State Path Wrong
mission.objective: Fix the `config.path` so it points to the state file created by the validate script and `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A `terraform_remote_state` data source is configured correctly, but the output references a key that does not exist in the remote state.
mission.name: Wrong Output Key
mission.objective: Fix the output key to `vpc_id` so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A `for` expression tries to filter data source content directly, but the content is a string. It must be decoded with `jsondecode` first.
mission.name: String Is Not a List
mission.objective: Wrap the data source content in `jsondecode()` before filtering so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: A data source may not find the target file, and the output has no null/error guard. Fix it to handle the missing case gracefully.
mission.name: Missing File, Missing Guard
mission.objective: Wrap the data source access in `try()` to provide a default value when the file is missing, so `terraform plan` succeeds.

mission.description: The config uses `terraform.workspace` to build a filename, but there is a typo: `terraform.workpsace` instead of `terraform.workspace`.
mission.name: Workspace Typo
mission.objective: Fix the typo so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A workspace conditional is missing quotes around the string `"default"`, causing a parse error.
mission.name: Unquoted String in Condition
mission.objective: Fix the condition so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A workspace conditional checks for `"prodution"` (missing the 'c'), so it never matches the actual workspace name `"production"`.
mission.name: Production Misspelled
mission.objective: Fix the typo so the count conditional works correctly and `terraform plan` passes.

mission.description: A `locals` block builds a config map and tries to look up the current workspace's value. The lookup syntax is wrong.
mission.name: Map Lookup Gone Wrong
mission.objective: Fix the map access syntax so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `count` expression references `workspace` without the required `terraform.` prefix.
mission.name: Missing terraform. Prefix
mission.objective: Add the `terraform.` prefix so `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The backend `path` attribute tries to use `${terraform.workspace}` interpolation, which is not allowed in backend blocks.
mission.name: No Interpolation in Backend
mission.objective: Remove the invalid interpolation and use a static path. Workspaces automatically separate state. `terraform init` must succeed.

mission.description: Two resources share the same output filename regardless of workspace. Adding the workspace name to the filename prevents collisions when both workspaces run in the same directory.
mission.name: Name Collision Across Workspaces
mission.objective: Add `terraform.workspace` as a suffix to the resource filename so `terraform plan` passes and names are unique per workspace.

mission.description: A `for_each` uses a map keyed by workspace names, but the `default` workspace is missing from the map.
mission.name: Missing Workspace Key in Map
mission.objective: Add the `default` key to the map so `terraform plan` succeeds in the default workspace.

mission.description: A module receives its environment name from a workspace-keyed map, but the current workspace is not in the map.
mission.name: Module Missing Workspace Key
mission.objective: Add the missing workspace key to the map so the module input resolves and `terraform plan` passes.

mission.description: A variable used to hold the workspace name has no default value, causing `terraform plan` to require interactive input.
mission.name: Variable Default Missing
mission.objective: Add `default = "default"` to the variable so `terraform plan` works non-interactively.

mission.description: Resource B reads a file created by resource A, but the path uses a hardcoded workspace name instead of `terraform.workspace`, breaking the reference in all workspaces except `default`.
mission.name: Wrong Dependency Path
mission.objective: Fix the path in resource B to use `terraform.workspace` so the reference resolves correctly in any workspace and `terraform plan` passes.

mission.description: The backend block uses `${terraform.workspace}` inside the path, which is not allowed. Backend blocks must have static configuration.
mission.name: Invalid Backend Interpolation
mission.objective: Remove the interpolation from the backend block so `terraform init` succeeds.

mission.description: A test file uses `tests {}` as the top-level block, but that is not a valid block in `.tftest.hcl` files. Terraform test files use `run {}` blocks.
mission.name: Wrong Block in the Test File
mission.objective: Fix the block type from `tests` to `run` so that `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: A `run` block sets `command = "apply_all"`, which is not a valid command value. Only `apply` and `plan` are allowed.
mission.name: Invalid Run Command
mission.objective: Fix the command value so that `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: The test asserts that `output.result == "wrong_value"`, but the actual output is `"correct_value"`. The assertion always fails.
mission.name: Wrong Expected Value in Assert
mission.objective: Fix the `assert` condition so it matches the actual output and `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: The `assert` block has `error_message = ""` — an empty string. Terraform requires a non-empty error message in every assert.
mission.name: Empty Error Message
mission.objective: Add a meaningful error message so the assert is valid and `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: A test uses `expect_failures = ["var.port"]` (a string) to confirm a validation error fires, but `expect_failures` requires unquoted references, not strings.
mission.name: Wrong expect_failures Address
mission.objective: Correct the `expect_failures` entry to an unquoted reference so `terraform test` confirms the validation failure.

mission.description: The test file overrides `var.item_count` with `"three"` (a string), but the variable is declared as `type = number`. Terraform rejects the type mismatch.
mission.name: Wrong Type in Test Variable Override
mission.objective: Fix the variable override so it passes a number and `terraform test` succeeds.

mission.description: The second `run` block references `run.first.output.file_path`, which is not valid syntax. Outputs from previous runs are accessible directly as `output.<name>`.
mission.name: Wrong Output Reference Across Run Blocks
mission.objective: Fix the output reference so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: A `run` block uses `command = "plan"` but asserts an output value that is only known after apply. During plan, the output is `(known after apply)` and the assertion always fails.
mission.name: Asserting Applied Values During Plan
mission.objective: Change the command to `"apply"` so the output value is known and the assertion can succeed.

mission.description: A test uses `mock_provider "local" {}` but does not define a `mock_resource` for `local_file`. Terraform cannot mock the resource schema and the test fails.
mission.name: Incomplete Mock Provider
mission.objective: Add a `mock_resource "local_file"` with default values so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: `override_resource { target = local_file.wrong_name }` references a resource that does not exist. Fix the address to match the actual resource.
mission.name: Wrong Resource Address in override_resource
mission.objective: Correct the `target` address in `override_resource` so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: `override_data { target = data.local_file.wrong }` uses an incorrect data source address. Fix it to match the actual data source.
mission.name: Wrong Data Source Address in override_data
mission.objective: Correct the `target` address in `override_data` so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: The main config calls a local module with `source = "../wrong/path"`. The module does not exist at that path, so `terraform test` fails.
mission.name: Wrong Module Source Path in Test
mission.objective: Fix the module source path so `terraform test` can find the child module.

mission.description: The test tries to compare a sensitive output directly: `condition = output.password == "secret123"`. Terraform refuses to evaluate sensitive values in equality conditions. Fix the assertion to check only that the output is non-empty.
mission.name: Asserting a Sensitive Output Value
mission.objective: Rewrite the assert condition to avoid direct comparison of the sensitive value.

mission.description: The test file configures the `local` provider twice using `provider` blocks. Terraform rejects duplicate provider configurations. Remove the duplicate.
mission.name: Duplicate Provider Configuration in Test
mission.objective: Remove the duplicate `provider` block so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: The assert uses `condition = output.a == "x" && output.b == "wrong"`. The second part is always false because `output.b` is `"y"`, not `"wrong"`. Fix both parts of the compound condition.
mission.name: Compound Assertion Always False
mission.objective: Correct the compound assertion so it accurately tests both outputs and `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: The test asserts `output.files["wrong_key"].content` but the `for_each` map uses keys `"alpha"` and `"beta"`. Fix the key in the assertion.
mission.name: Wrong Key in for_each Output Assertion
mission.objective: Use the correct map key in the assertion so `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: `expect_failures = [local_file.config]` targets the resource but the validation check is on `var.filename`. Fix the target to `var.filename`.
mission.name: Wrong expect_failures Target for Precondition
mission.objective: Correct the `expect_failures` target so it points to the variable with the validation and `terraform test` passes.

mission.description: A two-run test: `run "setup"` applies first, then `run "check"` asserts `output.manifest_path`. But `manifest_path` references `local_file.manifest`, which does not exist in `main.tf`. Add the missing resource.
mission.name: Missing Resource Referenced in Assertion
mission.objective: Add the `local_file.manifest` resource and its output to `main.tf` so the multi-run test passes.

mission.description: An output exposes `random_password.db.result` without marking it `sensitive = true`. The raw password will be printed to the terminal and stored in state in plaintext output.
mission.name: Sensitive Output Leak
mission.objective: Add `sensitive = true` to the output so the password is redacted and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: A `locals` block assigns a sensitive variable to a local. Terraform automatically propagates sensitivity through locals. However, the output wraps it in `nonsensitive()`, stripping the protection. Fix it by removing `nonsensitive()`.
mission.name: nonsensitive() Stripping Sensitivity
mission.objective: Remove `nonsensitive()` from the output so sensitivity is properly preserved and `terraform validate` passes.

mission.description: The output directly wraps a sensitive variable in `nonsensitive()`, exposing it. Fix it: remove `nonsensitive()` and mark the output as `sensitive = true`.
mission.name: Direct nonsensitive() on Secret Variable
mission.objective: Remove `nonsensitive()` and add `sensitive = true` to the output so the secret is protected.

mission.description: `terraform.tfvars` contains `db_password = "supersecret123"`. The config references it in a plain (non-sensitive) output, which will print the value. Fix: mark the output as `sensitive`.
mission.name: Secret in tfvars Exposed via Output
mission.objective: Add `sensitive = true` to the output so the secret from tfvars is redacted.

mission.description: The variable is named `DB_PASSWORD` (uppercase), but Terraform environment variable injection requires `TF_VAR_db_password` (lowercase). The name mismatch means the env var is never read. Fix: rename the variable to `db_password`.
mission.name: Wrong Variable Name for TF_VAR_ Injection
mission.objective: Rename the variable to `db_password` so it maps to the `TF_VAR_db_password` environment variable.

mission.description: `random_password.db.result` is written to a `local_file` resource, creating a plaintext credentials file. Fix: use `local_sensitive_file` instead to enforce stricter file permissions.
mission.name: Password Written to Plaintext File
mission.objective: Replace `local_file` with `local_sensitive_file` so the credentials file is created with restrictive permissions.

mission.description: `tls_locally_signed_cert` references `ca_key_algorithm = "RSA"` (a hardcoded string) instead of `tls_private_key.ca.algorithm`. Fix the reference.
mission.name: Wrong ca_key_algorithm in TLS Cert Chain
mission.objective: Replace the hardcoded string with the correct reference to `tls_private_key.ca.algorithm` so `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: `tls_self_signed_cert` with `validity_period_hours = 1` expires in one hour and `early_renewal_hours = 0` means no automatic renewal buffer. Fix: set `validity_period_hours = 8760` (1 year) and `early_renewal_hours = 168` (1 week).
mission.name: TLS Certificate Expiring Too Fast
mission.objective: Set appropriate validity and early renewal hours so the cert is long-lived and will renew with enough lead time.

mission.description: The `random_password` resource has `keepers = { always_rotate = timestamp() }`. Because `timestamp()` changes on every plan, the password rotates on every apply. Fix: use a stable keeper value.
mission.name: Password Forced to Rotate on Every Apply
mission.objective: Replace the volatile `timestamp()` keeper with a stable value so the password only rotates when intentionally triggered.

mission.description: `local_sensitive_file` is created with `file_permission = "777"`, which grants everyone on the system read, write, and execute access. Fix: set `file_permission = "0600"`.
mission.name: Overly Permissive File Permissions
mission.objective: Change `file_permission` to `"0600"` so only the owner can read and write the file.

mission.description: `prevent_destroy = true` is hardcoded, blocking destruction in every workspace including dev and test. Fix: use `terraform.workspace == "production"` so only the production workspace is protected.
mission.name: Unconditional prevent_destroy Blocks All Environments
mission.objective: Make `prevent_destroy` conditional on the workspace so dev/test can be destroyed freely.

mission.description: `ignore_changes = [content]` is configured on a credentials file. If someone manually edits or corrupts the file content, Terraform will never detect or correct it. Remove `ignore_changes` for the security-critical `content` attribute.
mission.name: ignore_changes Hiding Security Drift
mission.objective: Remove `ignore_changes = [content]` so Terraform will detect and correct drift in the credentials file.

mission.description: The variable validation uses `condition = length(var.password) <= 8`, which accepts short passwords and rejects long ones — the opposite of a security requirement. Fix: change `<=` to `>=`.
mission.name: Wrong Operator in Password Length Validation
mission.objective: Correct the validation operator so passwords shorter than 8 characters are rejected.

mission.description: A resource precondition uses `condition = var.env != "production"`, which blocks the resource from being created in production. The intention is to allow dev, staging, and production. Fix: use `contains(["dev","staging","production"], var.env)`.
mission.name: Precondition Blocks Production Deployment
mission.objective: Fix the precondition so it allows valid environments including production.

mission.description: A postcondition asserts `self.file_permission == "0644"` but the resource creates the file with `file_permission = "0600"`. The postcondition will always fail. Fix: align the postcondition with the actual permission.
mission.name: Postcondition File Permission Mismatch
mission.objective: Change the postcondition to check `"0600"` so it matches the resource and `terraform apply` succeeds.

mission.description: A sensitive variable is passed into a `local_file` content (not `local_sensitive_file`), and the output does not mark it sensitive. The sensitive value leaks through the output. Fix both issues.
mission.name: Sensitive Variable Passed Without Protection
mission.objective: Use `local_sensitive_file` and mark the output `sensitive = true` so the secret is fully protected.

mission.description: The `terraform.tf` file contains a comment with a hardcoded access key `AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`. Even in a comment, credentials in source control are a security violation. Remove the hardcoded credential from the config.
mission.name: Hardcoded Secret in Backend Config Comment
mission.objective: Remove the hardcoded credential from the config file so no secret appears in source.

mission.description: `random_password.result` is wrapped in `nonsensitive()` and written to a `local_file`. Both issues must be fixed: remove `nonsensitive()` and use `local_sensitive_file`.
mission.name: Password Exposed via nonsensitive() to Plain File
mission.objective: Fix both the `nonsensitive()` misuse and the insecure file resource so the password is fully protected.

mission.description: Two `provider "local"` blocks exist — one aliased `primary` and one aliased `secondary`. A resource references `provider = local.wrong`, which doesn't exist.
mission.name: Alias Confusion
mission.objective: Fix the provider reference so the resource uses `provider = local.primary`.

mission.description: A resource sets `provider = "local.primary"` using a string literal. Terraform requires a provider reference (not a string) for this meta-argument.
mission.name: String vs Reference
mission.objective: Fix the `provider` meta-argument syntax from a string to a proper reference.

mission.description: Two resources share the same static filename and both use `create_before_destroy = true`. When Terraform tries to replace them, a name collision occurs.
mission.name: Name Collision on Replacement
mission.objective: Make the filenames unique so that replacement succeeds without collision.

mission.description: A lifecycle block uses `replace_triggered_by = [null_resource.wrong_ref]`, but no resource named `null_resource.wrong_ref` exists in the configuration.
mission.name: Triggered by Nothing
mission.objective: Fix the `replace_triggered_by` to reference a resource that actually exists.

mission.description: A resource was renamed from `local_file.old` to `local_file.new`, but the `moved` block has `from` and `to` swapped — it points from `new` to `old` instead of the correct direction.
mission.name: Moving in the Wrong Direction
mission.objective: Fix the `moved` block so Terraform maps the old state address to the new resource name without destroying and recreating.

mission.description: A `moved` block migrates a resource into a child module, but the module name in the `to` address is wrong — it says `module.wrong_module` instead of `module.storage`.
mission.name: Module Migration Mismatch
mission.objective: Fix the `moved` block's `to` address to use the correct module name.

mission.description: A `moved` block migrates `local_file.items[0]` (count-based) to `local_file.items["primary"]` (for_each-based), but the string key `primary` is missing its quotes.
mission.name: Key Quoting in moved Block
mission.objective: Add the missing quotes around the for_each instance key in the `moved` block.

mission.description: A `removed` block is used to tell Terraform to forget about `local_file.old` without destroying it, but the resource is still declared in the config — causing a conflict.
mission.name: Ghost Resource
mission.objective: Remove the `resource` block for `local_file.old` from the config, keeping only the `removed` block.

mission.description: An `import` block uses `to = module.storage.local_file.config`, but the `module.storage` module does not exist in this configuration. The resource should be imported directly.
mission.name: Wrong Import Destination
mission.objective: Fix the `import` block's `to` address to point to `local_file.config` directly.

mission.description: An `import` block provides `id = 12345` as a number literal. The `id` argument must always be a string.
mission.name: ID Type Mismatch
mission.objective: Fix the `id` in the `import` block to be a valid string path.

mission.description: An output block has a `postcondition` that uses `self.wrong_attr` — but the correct attribute for an output's self reference is `self.value`.
mission.name: Self-Referential Error
mission.objective: Fix the postcondition to use `self.value` instead of `self.wrong_attr`.

mission.description: A resource has a `precondition` that requires `var.env == "production"`, but the default value for `var.env` is `"dev"`, causing the plan to always fail.
mission.name: Too Strict a Gate
mission.objective: Fix the precondition so it accepts any valid environment value: dev, staging, or production.

mission.description: A double-nested `dynamic` block uses the default iterator name for both the outer and inner loops. The inner iterator shadows the outer, making the outer iterator inaccessible inside the inner block.
mission.name: Iterator Identity Crisis
mission.objective: Give the inner `dynamic` block a unique `iterator` name so both levels are accessible.

mission.description: A `check` block asserts that `local_file.config.id != ""`, but the `id` attribute for `local_file` may not be the meaningful non-empty indicator. The correct attribute to check is `.filename`.
mission.name: Always Failing Assertion
mission.objective: Fix the `check` block assertion to use `local_file.config.filename != ""`.

mission.description: A `random_password` is generated and its result is written directly to a `local_file`. The password is exposed in plain text. Fix this by using `local_sensitive_file` and marking the output as sensitive.
mission.name: Secrets Leaking into State
mission.objective: Switch to `local_sensitive_file` and add `sensitive = true` to the output.

mission.description: A resource uses `ignore_changes = all`, which causes Terraform to ignore ALL attribute changes — including security-critical ones like `file_permission`. Fix this by using a specific attribute list.
mission.name: Ignoring Everything (Including Security)
mission.objective: Replace `ignore_changes = all` with a specific list that only ignores `content`.

mission.description: A precondition is meant to ensure `var.min_size` is less than `var.max_size`, but the condition is written with `>` instead of `<`, inverting the logic.
mission.name: Backwards Logic
mission.objective: Fix the precondition so it correctly validates that `min_size < max_size`.

mission.description: The `.terraform.lock.hcl` file contains an invalid provider hash, causing `terraform init` to fail with a hash mismatch error.
mission.name: Corrupted Lock File
mission.objective: Delete the corrupted lock file so `terraform init -upgrade` can regenerate it correctly.

mission.description: Three resources are being migrated from `count` to `for_each`. Multiple `moved` blocks are present but all use incorrect instance key formats — unquoted identifiers instead of quoted string keys.
mission.name: The Great Migration
mission.objective: Fix all three `moved` blocks to use correct for_each string key format.

mission.description: An auth token variable has a `validation` block with an overly strict regex that rejects valid token formats. The regex only allows lowercase hex, but real tokens contain uppercase letters and hyphens.
mission.name: Token Validation Trap
mission.objective: Fix the variable validation regex to accept alphanumeric characters and hyphens, 32-128 characters long.

mission.description: A configuration has a broken provider source that causes `terraform init` to fail. The validate.sh uses `TF_LOG=DEBUG` to surface more detail. Fix the provider source so `terraform init` succeeds.
mission.name: Reading the Debug Logs
mission.objective: Correct the provider source from a fake registry to `hashicorp/local`.

mission.description: The `local_file` resource has `file_permission = 644` (a number), but the provider requires a string. The error message from the provider tells you exactly what to fix.
mission.name: Wrong Attribute Type
mission.objective: Fix `file_permission` to be the string `"0644"`.

mission.description: A `null_resource` has a trigger that references `local_file.nonexistent.id` — a resource that is not declared in the configuration. This causes `terraform plan` to fail.
mission.name: Plan Failure Forensics
mission.objective: Fix the trigger to reference a resource that actually exists in the config.

mission.description: Two resources exist. The first is valid; the second has `file_permission = 999` which is not a valid octal permission string, causing it to fail on apply. Fix the second resource so the full apply succeeds.
mission.name: Partial Apply Recovery
mission.objective: Fix `file_permission = 999` to a valid octal string like `"0644"`.

mission.description: `local_file.a` content references `local_file.b.filename` and `local_file.b` content references `local_file.a.filename`, creating a dependency cycle. Fix by using a local value to break the cycle.
mission.name: The Infinite Loop
mission.objective: Break the cycle by introducing a `local` value that both resources can reference without circular dependency.

mission.description: A `random_string` result is used as the `count` value for a `local_file` resource. Since `random_string.result` is unknown until apply, Terraform cannot determine how many resources to plan.
mission.name: Unknown at Plan Time
mission.objective: Replace the unknown `count` value with a static integer.

mission.description: A `local_file` resource uses `content = timestamp()`. Since `timestamp()` returns a different value on every plan, Terraform always sees a diff and will never converge.
mission.name: The Never-Ending Plan
mission.objective: Fix the perpetual diff by using `lifecycle { ignore_changes = [content] }` or a static content value.

mission.description: The `.terraform.lock.hcl` contains an incorrect hash for the `local` provider, causing `terraform init` to fail with a hash verification error.
mission.name: Lock File Hash Conflict
mission.objective: Delete the lock file so `terraform init` can regenerate it with the correct hashes.

mission.description: The `required_providers` block specifies a provider from a fake registry `notarealregistry.example.com/fake/provider`. `terraform init` fails because this provider does not exist.
mission.name: Provider Not Found
mission.objective: Replace the fake provider with the real `hashicorp/local` provider.

mission.description: Two local modules in the same configuration require incompatible version constraints for the `local` provider: one requires `~> 2.4` and the other requires `>= 3.0`. These constraints cannot be satisfied simultaneously.
mission.name: Version Constraint Clash
mission.objective: Align the provider version constraints in both modules so they are compatible.

mission.description: A stale `terraform.tfstate` file is present that records `local_file.config` as existing, but the config tries to create it fresh. The state inconsistency causes an error. Fix: delete the stale state and apply cleanly.
mission.name: Ghost in the State
mission.objective: Remove the stale state file so `terraform apply` creates the resource from scratch.

mission.description: An `import` block tries to import `local_file.config` using the wrong address — it references `local_file.wrong_resource`. Fix the `to` address to match the declared resource.
mission.name: Already in State
mission.objective: Correct the `import` block's `to` address from `local_file.wrong_resource` to `local_file.config`.

mission.description: A `local` value accesses `data.local_file.maybe.content`, but the data source may fail if the file doesn't exist, propagating an error. Fix this by using `try()` to provide a default value.
mission.name: Handling the Absent Value
mission.objective: Wrap the data source attribute access in `try()` to return a default string when the file is absent.

mission.description: A `for_each` uses a sensitive variable value as the map key. Terraform prohibits sensitive values as `for_each` keys because they would be exposed in the plan output. Fix by using `nonsensitive()` on the key.
mission.name: Sensitive Keys Forbidden
mission.objective: Wrap the sensitive key with `nonsensitive()` so it can be used as a `for_each` key.

mission.description: A `for_each` uses a map derived from `random_string` results as keys. Since `random_string.result` is unknown until apply, the `for_each` keys are unknown at plan time — which Terraform does not allow.
mission.name: Unknown for_each Keys
mission.objective: Replace the unknown `for_each` key with a predetermined, static key.

mission.description: A chain of four resources (A→B→C→D) exists, where D references A's output. But resource A (`local_file.base`) is not declared in the config — only B, C, and D are. Fix by adding the missing A resource declaration.
mission.name: Missing Link in the Chain
mission.objective: Add the missing `local_file.base` resource declaration so the dependency chain is complete.

mission.description: A local value uses `tolist(tomap(["a","b","c"]))` — converting a list to a map requires key-value pairs, not a plain list. This causes a type conversion error.
mission.name: Type Conversion Tangle
mission.objective: Fix the function chain to correctly create a list of strings without invalid type conversions.

mission.description: A resource uses `count = -1`, which is an invalid value. Terraform rejects negative counts with a clear error. Fix by setting `count = 1`.
mission.name: Negative Count Crash
mission.objective: Change `count = -1` to `count = 1` to produce a valid configuration.

mission.description: A config was written to create 10 random_string resources for load testing, but someone accidentally set count = 0, creating nothing. The inline comment also gives wrong advice about -parallelism. Fix the count and understand why parallelism matters for large configs.
mission.name: Parallelism Tuning
mission.objective: Fix the resource count so all 10 random_string resources are created. terraform apply must succeed.

mission.description: Three resources A, B, and C exist in the config. C depends on A. The config is broken because resource C references the wrong attribute of A. Fix the attribute reference so the dependency chain is correct and both a targeted apply of A and a full apply succeed.
mission.name: Targeted Operations
mission.objective: Fix the attribute reference in resource C so that `terraform apply -target` and then `terraform apply` both succeed.

mission.description: A resource was configured with `lifecycle { ignore_changes = all }` which masks a real configuration issue. The broken config uses ignore_changes incorrectly — it hides ALL changes instead of only the specific attribute that should be ignored. Fix the lifecycle block to only ignore the `keepers` attribute, then verify plan with -refresh=false succeeds.
mission.name: The Stale State Problem
mission.objective: Fix lifecycle ignore_changes to only ignore the `keepers` attribute, then verify plan with -refresh=false succeeds.

mission.description: A resource is configured without a lifecycle block to prevent unintended recreation. The validate script applies the config and then uses -refresh-only to update state. The broken config is missing the lifecycle block that prevents resource recreation when keepers change. Without it, any keeper change causes a destroy-and-recreate.
mission.name: Refresh-Only Mode
mission.objective: Add a lifecycle block with ignore_changes = [keepers] to prevent recreation on keeper drift, then verify refresh-only works.

mission.description: A large config has been split into two: config-a (infrastructure) and config-b (application). Config-b reads config-a's state via terraform_remote_state, but references the wrong output key. Fix the output key reference so config-b can correctly consume config-a's outputs.
mission.name: State Partitioning
mission.objective: Fix the wrong output key in config-b's remote_state reference so both configs can be applied.

mission.description: A monolithic main.tf with 5 resources has been refactored into a child module. However, the `moved` blocks are missing from the root config, so Terraform will plan to destroy all 5 original resources and recreate them inside the module. Add the missing moved blocks to make the refactor zero-destructive.
mission.name: Module Splitting with moved Blocks
